Based on 0.8–2.2 g per kg of body weight per day. This is general guidance, not medical advice.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter your body weight in kg or lb.
  2. Pick the activity level that matches your lifestyle.
  3. Read your daily protein target and how to split it across meals.

❓ Frequently asked questions

Why is protein measured per kg of body weight?

Research-backed ranges (1.2-2.2 g/kg for active people, 0.8 g/kg minimum for sedentary adults) scale with body size, so heavier people need more.

Can I eat too much protein?

Healthy kidneys handle high intakes well, but there is little benefit above ~2.2 g/kg for muscle building. Spread intake across 3-5 meals for best use.

What counts toward the target?

All dietary protein: meat, fish, eggs, dairy, legumes, tofu, nuts and protein powders.
